course_title: Special Topics in Korean: Korean Foodways
subject: KRN
course_description: Study of Korean language, literature, society, thought, or culture, alone or in conjunction with other literary or cultural trends. Topics to be announced in advance.
course_notes: This course explores Korean culture and society through the lens of foodways, i.e., various forms of cultural practices involved in the production, distribution, and consumption of food. Food is not only about nutrition but can also entail symbolic meanings associated with cultural values and social structures. Approaching food as a symbolic system, this course discusses issues of nationalism, globalization, commodification, cultural relativism, identity, gender, class, and so forth in and beyond Korea. Drawing on scholarly articles, novels, and films, students will learn how food serves as a dynamic site of cultural reproduction and transformation through case studies of Korea. Students will conduct group ethnographic projects on Korean food to connect class discussions with real-life experiences around themselves.
